title: The Baby and the Boat
description: A story my father, Walter Thompson, told.

texts:
The Baby and the Boat

A story my father told.

My Dad, Walter Thompson, retold this story to me as we sat on his front porch in Kingston.

Here's what I remember.

My Dad roomed with the Dookie family.

He was good friends with my Uncle Felix Dookie, and I think that's how he came to meet my mom, Mabel.

My Dad would shave grandpa Dookie regularly.

"Every time I shaved grandpa Dookie," my Dad said, "grandpa Dookie would tell the same story."

Grandpa Dookie and his young wife were taken to Jamaica on a very crowded boat

(most likely a ship).

On the boat was another young couple, and the wife was pregnant.

While at sea, she gave birth on the boat.
The boat was so crowded, passengers had to transfer to another, less crowded boat.
While crossing over to the new boat, the newborn baby was carried down a ladder.

Someone let the baby slip,

and the baby fell into the sea.
Grandpa Dookie told the same story every time Walter shaved him, and would end with the same refrain:

"De baby born a sea, an the baby die a sea."

(The baby born at sea, and the baby died at sea.)
